Let h∗ (G) denote the generalized Fitting height of a finite group G defined
as the minimum number k such that Fk∗ (G) = G, where F1∗ (G) = F ∗ (G) is the
                                                       ∗
generalized Fitting subgroup of G, and by induction Fi+1  (G) is the inverse image of
  ∗      ∗                            ∗
F (G/Fi (G)). If G is soluble, then h (G) = h(G) is the Fitting height of G.
    Does every finite group G contain a soluble subgroup K such that h∗ (G) = h(K)?
                                                                          P. Shumyatsky
